record.paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
record.context_brief: Heavy-tail behavior outside the conjectured regime
record.original_question: In critically loaded finite-capacity GI/G/1/K queues, what explains the apparent split between heavy-tailed Weibull and light-tailed examples, which seem to agree with Conjecture 1, and Lognormal and Pareto examples, which appear to behave differently? Is the discrepancy for Lognormal and Pareto caused by very slow convergence of γ*(t) to γ* as t → ∞, by the finite-buffer correction term vanishing much more slowly than 1/K as K → ∞, or by a genuinely different asymptotic limit for those distributions?

evidence.quote: The figure indicates that Lognormal and Pareto distributions exhibit one type of behavior (having a BRAVO effect but possibly not with a factor of 1/3) and in contrast the heavy-tailed Weibull exhibits behaviors similar to light-tailed distributions as in Conjecture 1.

Note also that it is possible that for the Lognormal and the Pareto distributions which we simulate, either the convergence of γ ∗(t) to γ ∗ is very slow as t → ∞, or perhaps the oK(1) term which we conjecture to be O(1/K) for light-tailed distributions, vanishes at a much slower rate as K → ∞, with these distributions.
Open Problem Heavy-tailed Weibull and light-tailed distributions exhibit one type of behavior, in agreement with Conjecture 1. Lognormal and Pareto exhibit a different behavior.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a GI/G/1/K queue: a single-server queue with i.i.d. interarrival times having distribution A and i.i.d. service times having distribution B (independent of arrivals), a single server working at unit rate, and a finite buffer of capacity K (customers arriving when the system holds K customers are lost). Assume the queue is critically loaded, i.e., E[A] = E[B] =: 1/λ, and that A and B have finite second moments with squared coefficients of variation c_a^2 and c_s^2. Let D(t) denote the number of customer departures (service completions) by time t in stationarity, and define the asymptotic variance rate
   γ*(K) := lim_{t→∞} Var(D(t))/t,
and the time-dependent variance rate γ*(t,K) := Var(D(t))/t.

A widely studied conjecture (the BRAVO conjecture for critically loaded GI/G/1/K queues) asserts that, for sufficiently light-tailed interarrival/service distributions,
   γ*(K) = λ (c_a^2 + c_s^2)/3 + o_K(1) as K → ∞,
with the correction term o_K(1) believed to be of order O(1/K).

Empirical simulation evidence indicates that:
 (i) heavy-tailed Weibull (with shape parameter < 1) interarrival/service distributions and light-tailed distributions appear to obey the formula above;
 (ii) Lognormal and Pareto interarrival/service distributions appear to deviate, in that the simulated γ*(t,K) does not converge to λ(c_a^2+c_s^2)/3 within the studied ranges of t and K.

Determine which of the following explains the observed deviation for Lognormal and Pareto distributions:
 (a) the conjectured limit γ*(K) → λ(c_a^2+c_s^2)/3 still holds, but the convergence γ*(t,K) → γ*(K) as t → ∞ is genuinely very slow;
 (b) the conjectured limit holds for each fixed K, but the finite-buffer correction γ*(K) − λ(c_a^2+c_s^2)/3 vanishes much more slowly than 1/K as K → ∞;
 (c) the asymptotic limit lim_{K→∞} γ*(K) is genuinely different from λ(c_a^2+c_s^2)/3 for these distributions, so that the BRAVO 1/3 factor fails in this regime.

Provide a proof identifying the correct alternative, together with rigorous rates (for (a) the rate of convergence in t; for (b) the rate in K; for (c) the corrected limiting value).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about critically loaded GI/G/1/K queues with Lognormal and Pareto distributions. Subsequent literature (e.g., asymptotic variance results for GI/G/1 BRAVO under 2+ε moments, work on second-order terms of variance curves, and recent work on phase transitions and generalized BRAVO with oscillating cumulants) extends the BRAVO theory but does not appear to definitively resolve which of the three explanations (slow convergence in t, slow vanishing of the finite-buffer correction in K, or a genuinely different limit) accounts for the Lognormal/Pareto behavior. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Phase transitions and departure statistics of critically loaded queues: oscillating cumulants and generalized BRAVO
status_evidence.snippet: Cumulants of departure statistics deviate strongly from Poissonian values and oscillate near phase transitions at critical load, generalizing the BRAVO effect.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work generalizes BRAVO but does not specifically resolve the Lognormal/Pareto discrepancy in GI/G/1/K.

status_evidence.title: On busy periods of the critical GI/G/1 queue and BRAVO
status_evidence.snippet: Strengthens GI/G/1 BRAVO results under 2+ε moment assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: GI/G/1 BRAVO results have been refined, but the finite-buffer Lognormal/Pareto regime remains unsettled.

status_evidence.title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lognormal and Pareto exhibit a different behavior; open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The discrepancy is explicitly listed as an open problem.
